sources.title: Educational Resources / A Guide for Lighting the Stage
sources.source_bias: EDUCATIONAL_MATERIAL; theatre-oriented examples do not define concert practice.
sources.notes: Registry stores page metadata and concise normalized principles only.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Looking at the cue content
sources.source_bias: Console behavior only; does not prescribe lighting aesthetics.
sources.notes: Supports maintainability and handover reasoning, not external design rules.

sources.title: Define DMX Channels
sources.source_bias: Fixture-definition methodology; no guarantee that an external profile matches the loaded Show.
sources.notes: Use only after Show-bound identity/mode evidence is established.

sources.title: Fixture Information
sources.source_bias: Revision tags and uploaded profiles have different trust levels; user-uploaded data remains contextual.
sources.notes: Supports provenance and revision awareness for future fixture research.

sources.title: WL supports Paradise Under the Stars
sources.source_bias: One immersive-production case; designer statement is not a universal rule.
sources.notes: Retained as scope-bound professional practice.

sources.title: Jesse Lee Stout and Sooner Routhier Reflect Mood of Muse Tour
sources.source_bias: Large touring/music-video context; visual language and scale are case specific.
sources.notes: Retained as an industry reference, never as a K-pop or global recipe.

sources.title: Chauvet animates church's music video
sources.source_bias: Camera-oriented worship/pop-rock case with manufacturer and production framing.
sources.notes: Retained only for bounded alternative-strategy examples.

sources.title: A Guide for Lighting the Stage — Focus and Composition
sources.source_bias: Theatre education; concepts require adaptation for concert scale and camera context.
sources.notes: Used for bounded focus, composition, and audience-attention principles.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: What is Tracking
sources.source_bias: Console behavior and maintainability only; not an artistic prescription.
sources.notes: Supports tracking, cue-only, and release knowledge.

sources.title: grandMA2 Quick Start Guide: Editing a Sequence
sources.source_bias: Console workflow only; does not prescribe cue content.
sources.notes: Supports readable cue naming, timing, and operator edits.

sources.title: Chauvet keeps pace with Alice in Chains
sources.source_bias: Rock touring case; designer choices are specific to the band and venue scale.
sources.notes: Used for bounded darkness and musical responsiveness observations.

sources.title: Chauvet visuals fire up Enter Shikari
sources.source_bias: Rock/electronic touring case; fixture choices are not universal.
sources.notes: Used for bounded concentrated beam and stage-presence observations.

sources.title: Chauvet sets the mood for Muni Long
sources.source_bias: Pop performance case; gradients and strobe use are context-specific.
sources.notes: Used for bounded gradient and rhythm/body-language observations.

sources.title: Bigtime backs Black Keys Drop Out Boogie
sources.source_bias: Rock/blues touring case; changing fixture counts are not a universal energy rule.
sources.notes: Used for bounded resource variation and fundamentals observations.

sources.title: User-approved visual-language reference: restrained YG-like concert language
sources.source_bias: Personal preference layer; not industry consensus or a fixed recipe.
sources.notes: Human-confirmed design-language observations remain context-dependent and review-required.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Effects
sources.source_bias: Console behavior only; effect semantics do not prescribe when an artistic effect should be used.
sources.notes: Used for effect-type and maintainability knowledge.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Timecode
sources.source_bias: Console behavior only; does not establish artistic timing choices or whether a production should use timecode.
sources.notes: Used for timecode workflow and handover reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Executors
sources.source_bias: Console playback behavior only; does not prescribe page layout or operator workflow for every show.
sources.notes: Used for native playback and handover reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: MAtricks
sources.source_bias: Selection-order behavior only; it does not define an artistic distribution pattern.
sources.notes: Used to separate selection mechanics from design intent.

sources.title: GDTF Builder: Geometry Page
sources.source_bias: Describes fixture structure in a GDTF definition; does not prove that a particular loaded Show fixture matches that external file.
sources.notes: Used for geometry provenance and capability boundaries.

sources.title: GDTF Builder: Wheels Page
sources.source_bias: Describes how a GDTF file represents wheels; external definitions remain subordinate to Show-bound fixture identity and mode verification.
sources.notes: Used for color/gobo/prism/animation capability provenance.

sources.title: BTS Wrap Record-Setting 14-Month World Tour
sources.source_bias: Large-scale K-pop stadium/arena touring case; scale, budget, vendor network and bespoke systems are not representative of all productions.
sources.notes: Useful for scalable-show, continuity and K-pop touring context.

sources.title: Robe Adds Nuance To Hikaru Utada Science Fiction Tour Design
sources.source_bias: One high-budget J-pop arena production with a strong scenic/video concept and manufacturer-focused reporting.
sources.notes: Useful for mixed-media hierarchy, layering and spatial-lighting observations.

sources.title: Creating Pandemonium For The Pet Shop Boys, Part 1: The Designers' Roundtable
sources.source_bias: One pop/electronic touring production from 2009; technology has aged but design tradeoffs remain case evidence rather than universal rules.
sources.notes: Direct designer interview useful for restraint, video-light balance, color and tourability.

sources.title: Michael Bublé's Cool Summer Tour
sources.source_bias: One large outdoor pop/jazz touring case; palette, fixture choices and scenic vocabulary are artist-specific.
sources.notes: Useful for restraint, visual-language cohesion, daylight adaptation and movement discipline.

sources.title: Behind Labrinth’s Coachella Production With DX7 And PRG
sources.source_bias: Festival case with a specific artist and creative team; restrained choices are contextual, not a requirement for other shows.
sources.notes: Useful for deliberate stillness, scene-based pacing and precision-over-quantity evidence.

sources.title: 31 Days of Plots: Billie Eilish's Where Do We Go? World Tour
sources.source_bias: Large arena-tour design with extensive automation; song-specific rig movement is not transferable as a default technique.
sources.notes: Useful for song identity, automation and position-variation evidence.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Use variables in macros
sources.source_bias: Console macro/variable behavior only; does not establish that a Macro is the best abstraction for every repeated task.
sources.notes: Used for parameterized Macro and variable reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Command line interaction
sources.source_bias: Documents interactive Macro mechanics only; does not prescribe a user-facing workflow.
sources.notes: Used for interactive Macro and operator-input reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Clone
sources.source_bias: Documents cloning semantics; safe use still depends on current Show identity, target data, references, and intended scope.
sources.notes: Used for native transformation and adaptation reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Search and Replace
sources.source_bias: Documents search/replace capability; replacement can be destructive and requires bounded scope and verification.
sources.notes: Used for native batch-edit and inspection reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Apply worlds or filters to executors and sequences
sources.source_bias: Documents input/playback filtering behavior; does not establish which fixtures or attributes belong in a current Show filter.
sources.notes: Used for scope-control and reusable playback/programming reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Executor Options
sources.source_bias: Documents native playback options; does not prescribe one executor behavior or page architecture for every show.
sources.notes: Used to check native sequence/executor behavior before custom automation.

sources.title: LD and Programmer Michael Appel
sources.source_bias: One experienced programmer's workflow and collaboration perspective; not a universal staffing or programming rule.
sources.notes: Useful for programmer autonomy, editability, direction-following, and collaboration reasoning.

sources.title: Banks 'Serpentina' Tour
sources.source_bias: One artist-specific touring case with a distinct album world; mood and atmosphere decisions are contextual.
sources.notes: Useful for concept-to-lighting translation and atmosphere reasoning.

sources.title: Karol G $trip Love Tour
sources.source_bias: Large arena production with extensive automation, pyro and scenic coordination; scale and complexity are not transferable defaults.
sources.notes: Useful for rehearsal integration, precise timing and cross-department coordination evidence.

sources.title: Fantasia Barrino's Back to Me Tour
sources.source_bias: One artist-specific tour with period-based visual sections; palette and movement choices are narrative case evidence, not genre rules.
sources.notes: Useful for section-specific visual language, focus, color and movement reasoning.

sources.title: Having a crush on grandMA3
sources.source_bias: Interview is tied to one Crush arena production and grandMA3 workflow; design reasoning is transferable only where separated from MA3-specific feature semantics.
sources.notes: Direct interview with Lite Factory designer/programmer Soyoun Lee on narrative, rig restraint, spatial composition and console workflow.

sources.title: TWICE, This is For World Tour
sources.source_bias: Studio portfolio material presents its own production positively and describes a large-budget 360-degree arena case; details are not universal K-pop rules.
sources.notes: Useful for 360-degree audience geometry, multimedia layering and artist-vision integration.

sources.title: BLACKPINK - Coachella 2023 Concert Visuals
sources.source_bias: Visual-content studio portfolio; collaboration details are useful but do not independently establish lighting design rationale.
sources.notes: Useful as evidence of coordinated visual-content, creative, choreography, stage and lighting collaboration in a major K-pop performance.

sources.title: BTS THE COMEBACK LIVE | ARIRANG
sources.source_bias: First-person professional case study focused on key lighting and broadcast delivery for one high-profile production; not a universal concert workflow.
sources.notes: Useful for performer readability, broadcast exposure, rehearsal refinement and division-of-responsibility evidence.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Create pop-ups in macros
sources.source_bias: Documents Macro input prompts; does not establish that interactive prompts are desirable during live playback or safe without validation.
sources.notes: Used for interactive Macro input and secret/state hygiene reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 Release Notes 3.1: Plugins and Lua 5.3
sources.source_bias: Historical feature-introduction documentation; establishes intended plugin role but not current best practice for every automation problem.
sources.notes: Used for Macro-to-Lua escalation reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: ReloadPlugins Keyword
sources.source_bias: Documents Lua-engine reload and support/migration cautions; does not prohibit plugins when they are justified.
sources.notes: Used for plugin state, persistence, recovery and migration reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: Partial Show Read
sources.source_bias: Documents cross-show import capability; PSR can alter destination show data and requires source/destination mapping, scope and review.
sources.notes: Used for show-transfer, reuse, dependency and recovery reasoning.

sources.title: grandMA2 User Manual: How to do a Partial Show Read
sources.source_bias: Operational PSR procedure; merge/overwrite choices can be destructive and must not be inferred automatically.
sources.notes: Used for bounded import and backup-first reasoning.

sources.title: MDG CHATmosphere With Pierre Claude, Lighting Designer
sources.source_bias: One designer's strong minimalist aesthetic; useful as conditional practice, not a universal style rule.
sources.notes: Direct designer interview on restraint, synchronization, contrast and intentional exception.

sources.title: Mitski Be the Cowboy Tour with Elation Lighting
sources.source_bias: Tour case also discusses manufacturer equipment; artistic reasoning should be separated from product promotion.
sources.notes: Useful for choreography-first focus, static versus changing palette, and color removal.

sources.title: By Design: Bradley King Lights Hadestown
sources.source_bias: Theatre case rather than concert touring; transferable principles must remain contextual.
sources.notes: Useful for emotional color progression, design revision after failed previews, and multi-department visual collaboration.

sources.title: Xtylos and ReflectXion on Deftones North American Tour
sources.source_bias: Manufacturer marketing source promotes its products; only direct designer reasoning about negative space and composition is suitable as conditional evidence.
sources.notes: Useful for negative-space intent and avoiding full-stage wash.

sources.title: Lighting Designer Isabella Byrd Talks With City Theatrical
sources.source_bias: Theatre-oriented interview; restraint and rule-breaking concepts are transferable only as conditional design reasoning.
sources.notes: Useful for deliberate constraint, narrow palette and breaking self-imposed rules for impact.

sources.title: Bruce Springsteen and the E Street Band
sources.source_bias: One long-form touring case; useful for variation-on-theme and song-specific recipe reasoning, not a universal requirement that every song be visually unique.
sources.notes: Directly relevant to show-level variety without abandoning a consistent aesthetic.

sources.title: Karol G 'Mañana Será Bonito Tour'
sources.source_bias: Large stadium pop narrative case; chapter palette strategy is contextual and should not be generalized into fixed K-pop or pop rules.
sources.notes: Useful for multi-song chapter coherence inside a restricted palette and variation through intensity, timing and shade.

sources.title: Adele Live 2016 Tour
sources.source_bias: One artist-specific design with unusually restricted color; restraint is evidence of a valid strategy, not a rule against saturated color.
sources.notes: Useful for show identity through restriction and preserving rare saturated color for stronger impact.

sources.title: Jack White's Blue, Blue World
sources.source_bias: Artist-specific touring concept with an intentionally narrow blue-and-white language; not a universal palette strategy.
sources.notes: Useful for proving that a whole-show restricted palette can coexist with improvisation and song-level variation.

sources.title: Human feedback: multi-song color design should avoid template substitution without forcing novelty
sources.source_bias: Personal workflow and visual-quality evidence from a prior color-only multi-song test; not an industry-wide rule.
sources.notes: Owner observed that a roughly 12-song color-only output felt too formulaic because song differences were mostly parameter/color substitutions. Owner explicitly does not want either all songs to look the same or forced difference for its own sake.

sources.title: Elation Dartz For KISS End of the Road World Tour
sources.source_bias: Manufacturer-supported case promotes equipment; only direct designer statements about rehearsal-driven cue simplification are suitable as conditional design evidence.
sources.notes: Useful for over-programming detection and rehearsal-based cue subtraction.

sources.title: How Billie Eilish's Design Team Turned Her Dreams (and Nightmares) Into Realities
sources.source_bias: Artist-specific production with heavy video and timecode; detailed rhythmic accenting is contextual and not a rule to hit every beat.
sources.notes: Useful for song-persona identity, selective micro-detail accenting, and continuing refinement through deeper listening.
